content:
arjun: quick RFC follow-up — i'm proposing a "warmup + smoothing" policy for fp8/int8 rollouts so we don't get short-lived SLO blips when the quant path first sees real traffic. thoughts?

maya: sounds useful. can you show expected timelines and thresholds? how long is 'warmup'?

sasha: agree in principle. my worry is quality cliffs for certain prompt families during warmup. we should tie this to our degscore signal not just latency.

taylor: implementation question — do we apply warmup at routing time (route -> quantized replica but limit qps) or at runtime (gradual per-worker activation)? both have different cache priming implications.
arjun: good Qs. rough sketch below (config prototype):
```json
{"warmup_minutes": 15, "initial_traffic_pct": 0.02, "ramp_step_pct": 0.05, "ramp_interval_minutes": 5, "smoothing_window_minutes": 10, "degscore_threshold": 0.08, "quality_buffer_customers": ["enterprise-tier"], "fallback_delay_seconds": 30}
```

arjun: key points: start tiny (2%), step up 5% every 5m, but use a smoothing window to avoid flipping back/forth on noisy telemetry; fallback_delay to avoid thrashing for transient errors.

ops-bot: canary metrics (fp8-canary-2026-03-18): latency +7% p95, degscore +0.12 on the recv prompt-set — triggered partial rollback at 10% traffic.

maya: that canary number aligns w/ our concern. proposal: make smoothing_window adaptive — bigger during peak qps to avoid accidental rollbacks, smaller at low load so we can react faster.
sasha: +1 for adaptive. also suggest a "quality_buffer" flag per-customer that forces us to avoid quantized variants completely until warmup fully completes. default off for self-serve.
taylor: KV cache note: when new quant replicas come up they have cold caches, causing longer first-token latency. warmup at routing-level won't prime global kv — we should either pre-warm with synthetic traffic or account for a short cache penalty in the smoothing window.
arjun: agreed. add a pre-warm job that primes top n prefixes for the model for the first rollout wave. also capture first-10k requests separately for observability.
maya: ops action: can we add a metric that tags requests seen during warmup so we can compute warmup-specific degscore and latency?
arjun: yes — we add `rollout_phase: warmup|ramp|steady|fallback` tag to traces and logs.
sasha: edge-case: model variants that change output distribution (e.g., relying on different rounding) might show high degscore only after some rare prefix. we need a backstop: if degscore spikes above X and doesn't subside after 3 windows, auto-roll back and open a ticket.
taylor: agree. define X = 0.15 for now? we can tune.
arjun: action items: (1) implement rollout config schema + server-side enforcement (owner: arjun), (2) pre-warm job + priming list (owner: taylor), (3) telemetry tag + warmup dashboard (owner: maya), (4) safety rollback threshold + automation (owner: sasha). i'll open RFC follow-up PR with the config and a canary checklist.
maya: sounds good — will add dashboard template. :+1:
sasha: i'll draft the rollback playbook and thresholds.
taylor: i'll prototype the pre-warm job and run it against the next canary.
arjun: thanks — let's sync in the weekly eng-ml slot if anything blocks. :slightly_smiling_face:
